newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Brown returns fire over govt tax plans.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Brown returns fire over govt tax plans.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party finance spokesman, Gordon Brown, on Friday hit back at Conservative attacks on Labour's tax and spending plans, demanding to know how tax cuts announced in the Conservative manifesto would be paid for.
The ruling Conservatives have promised to cut income tax for married people who choose to stay at home to care for children or disabled relatives -- at a cost of 1.2 billion stg.
"Where would the 1.2 billion for their transferable tax allowance in the second year of the next parliament come from? The Chancellor would not tell us," Brown said.

Brown said Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke had also refused to divulge privatisation plans, adding that Clarke has said privatisation of London's underground railway service was not included in the government's plans for 1998/99 while Minister of Defence Michael Portillo had said it was.

"The Tories are in disarray on the public finances," Brown said. "And the question the Conservatives cannot answer is where is the money coming from to pay for their 15 billion stg tax and spending commitments."
Earlier, Clarke repeated Conservative claims that Labour's spending plans include a 12.0 billion stg "black hole".
Prime Minister John Major said a one penny cut in income tax, which kicks in this weekend, would quickly be reversed under a Labour government.
